For an accepted frame, every header field, both MAC addresses, the EtherType, the body and its padding, the 16-bit body sum and whether the header carries it, the Digidesign OUI test of the source address and the keepalive test are what the protocol grammar reads at the same offsets.

From the fields the grammar reads, the frame builder makes, in both sum modes, exactly the frame the harness builds itself from the protocol (sum or zero, padding to 60 bytes included); it refuses a body past 1484 bytes, a body holding the system family and a buffer one byte short, and writes nothing into a refused buffer.
The announce reader accepts only an e0 or e1 frame of at least 33 body bytes and reads the unknown bytes, the version and the name at their documented offsets, each cut and terminated as documented.
The session accepts every configuration the harness builds, each within the documented ranges.
Every frame the session sends is a well-formed frame from this host to the known desk, zero-padded to 60 bytes, with the right header sum, and never holds the system family F0 13 xx 70.
Each acknowledgement the session sends echoes the send counter of the desk frame it answers, with no body and retry 0.

A new data frame goes only while online, with nothing in flight and no back-off holding; a retransmission is the frame in flight again, byte for byte but its retry field, which counts 1, 2, ... never past the retry limit, and goes no sooner than the timeout; the acked notice names the frame in flight; the ack-lost notice comes for it after exactly the retry limit.

Online only after the desk acknowledges the wake frame and an e1 names this host since then; no wake frame while the desk is in a session with another host, and a wake returns the documented code; each desk announce notice carries the place of this host address, the desk type, the version and the name, and each desk data notice its body, counter and retry.
A keepalive goes only when due on its own clock, while online, with nothing in flight and no back-off holding: never early.

Each sent data frame stays within the command and body limits and carries the host counter advanced by its commands; with tagged commands, its count is right, it carries only commands submitted and still pending, and a frame with display writes follows the last by at least the configured gap.
Submit refuses a command holding F0 13 xx 70 and nothing else as such, and refuses for a full queue only when 512 commands are pending.
After each operation, the session has acknowledged each desk data frame owed an acknowledgement once each time it came, and no other frame.

After each operation, a wake frame went exactly when the host woke and a close frame exactly when owed; each desk data frame but a keepalive or a repeat, each announce and each foreign session was noticed as owed; and the state changed exactly as the header diagram says, in order, each change naming its reason.

After each operation, an acknowledgement of the frame in flight was taken and noticed, a frame in flight still unacknowledged after the timeout was sent again or dropped, and the reported deadline is from now to one second away and never later than the next retransmission.
After each operation, with tagged commands, a keepalive due while online with nothing in flight and no back-off holding has gone: never skipped.
With tagged commands, after each operation the queue holds exactly the pending commands in order, a newer command in its key place, and after a tick a command that may go has gone.

At most REAC_BOXREG_MAX_BOXES boxes, each of an even width of 2 to 40 (a rule the harness writes out itself) with its slice inside the fabric and a NUL-terminated name; no two slices overlap and no MAC is registered twice.
No call moves a box, changes its width or its pinned flag, unbinds or rebinds its MAC, or changes any name but the one set_name sets.

A declaration is refused for a bad width, a full table or no free range, and otherwise lands at the next index with the width asked for, at the pinned base or the lowest free range, pinned exactly when a base was given, unbound, with the name given; a refused one adds no box.

add refuses a bad width or the all-zero MAC, and otherwise gives the MAC's own box, then the first unbound box of that width, then a new unpinned box at the lowest free range; it is idempotent and find finds what it registered.
find answers -1 or the index of a box holding exactly that MAC, and never finds the all-zero MAC.
set_name stores the name given, or the empty name for NULL, at a valid index.
reac_ctrl_parse answers NONE exactly for a frame shorter than 50 bytes or not 0x8819, gives the same verdict with a NULL output, and its verdict is the kind it stores, which always has a name.

The parser reads the addresses and counter where the frame holds them and calls a frame FILLER exactly for type 00 00; the block and head-amp record checksum checks agree with sums the harness computes, and a head-amp record is only a link-4 SINGLE.

Both port decoders refuse the same blocks, leaving the output untouched; a decoded port table counts each slot code as its own kind in whole 4-channel slots, accounts for all twelve slots, names the first unknown code, and gives the head-amp base from the chassis strap.

An identity reply comes only from a frame with a closed block checksum, its payload lies where the record puts it inside the frame, its record checksum closes and its address is the record's own; a reassembled record lies inside the reassembly buffer, closes its checksum and carries the joined record's own address (its bytes 9 and 10), and a corrupt frame leaves the reassembly state unchanged.

The box classifier answers only for a Roland-OUI source that is not us, with a closed block checksum outside FILLER, and with one of its six events; only a config-announce matches a catalogue row, and it is the first row whose declaration is the frame's block.

Every block reac_ctrl_build_as emits for a catalogue row has a legal geometry and parses back as its kind; the config block's checksum closes, it is the row's declaration, the catalogue match recognises it and it declares the row's widths; its identity replies and reassembled records give the row's firmware, REAC version and, where the row has an identity record, model name.

The catalogue is not empty, the documented refusals of a bad argument hold (NULL pointers are refused, reac_ports_unknown clears its code, an out-of-range kind is named "?"), and an ingested model name is NUL-terminated.

Downstream: a frame is valid only as a 1492-byte 0x8819 frame ending C2 EA with its counter at bytes 14-15; reac_decode decodes exactly a valid frame of a fitting even-width geometry and reac_decode_plain_le a valid fitting one, each returning the samples per packet, a refused decode leaves its output untouched, and each plain-LE sample is the straight copy.
Decoding a frame's audio and braiding it again with reac_braid_encode gives back the audio region byte for byte, downstream and upstream, for a geometry of 12 samples or fewer.
Every decoded sample, downstream and upstream, is the three bytes the documented braid map puts it in, the map written out in the harness rather than taken from the library.

Upstream: reac_upstream_channels is the frame's geometry restricted to box widths, NULL arguments are refused, and reac_upstream_decode succeeds exactly on a 0x8819 frame of a box geometry ending C2 EA, leaving its output untouched when it refuses.

reac_frame_is_reac is true exactly for a frame of at least 14 bytes with EtherType 0x8819, and reac_frame_clean_len strips a two-byte FCS residue exactly when the length is two more than a legal geometry, and nothing else.

A sighting comes from a frame of at least 50 bytes, is the frame's own source and never our MAC, its geometry is the frame length's (at least that, for the hunt), its role is in range, outside FILLER its block checksum closes, and a declared width is at most REAC_MAX_CHANNELS.
The gate, the table and the hunt's table never hold more than REAC_DISCO_MAX peers or the same MAC twice, and every table role is in range.
An observe reports 0 or 1, the table's seq moves by that report plus one on the first refusal for room, and an entry the table holds as a box never becomes a master.

An observe changes the table as the harness calculates: a known entry takes each fact that sharpens it and the new time, reporting a change exactly when a fact changed; a new MAC gets an entry with the sighting's facts; a full table refuses a new MAC and marks itself overflowed.

Ageing removes exactly the entries a forward clock shows unheard for longer than the stale limit (none when the clock stepped back) and moves the table's seq on by one exactly when it removed some; a hunt step reports 0 or 1 and every verdict has a name.
Classify, the gate and the hunt's observe answer only their documented values, and the hunt never reports as a master a peer its table holds as a box.

A table always serialises into a buffer of REAC_DISCO_JSON_MAX bytes, and a successful serialisation is one NUL-terminated JSON array of the length returned with one object per entry, holding that entry's MAC, role, model, width, owned flag and age in ms.

A head-amp cell is set exactly when its channel and value are legal and then reads back as set, an unknown parameter has no value, and every unset cell carries the stated enrolling default: phantom off, pad off, and a SENS that is not zero.

A box is admitted, at the base and width it asked for, exactly when its slots are a positive width of at most REAC_GRANT_MAX_WIDTH inside the head-amp space; a refused one leaves the caller's allocation unchanged.
Every sweep row is a cd ea link-4 SINGLE block whose bytes from offset 2 sum to zero.

A group-A row, framed as a master stamps it, parses back as a HEADAMP record of its channel, parameter and the value the input last set for that cell (or the default), with its record and block checksums closed.

A sweep has REAC_GRANT_SWEEP_LEN rows or is refused for a smaller buffer; its two head frames are the measured ones byte for byte, its group-A rows are one per allocated channel per parameter in the measured order, and group B is the identity poll for the addresses and sizes the header names.
The sweep builder admits a hand-built allocation on the same terms as reac_grant_allocate and refuses NULL arguments.

The head-amp scheduler only emits a channel, parameter and value the table can hold, with the value the input last set (or the default), for a cell the input set or one inside the armed scene, and sends an unset cell at most once.

The decode reads no byte past the length it is given (a guard byte after the payload changes nothing), an ignored record changes nothing, and a well-formed firmware, REAC-version or model-name record is never ignored.

An accepted firmware reply is four decimal digits printed as D.DDD, a model name is the payload's text after its first byte, up to its first NUL or the name field's capacity, and never empty, and a REAC-version record keeps its eight bytes, decodes the last three words big-endian and prints as major.minor with a patch of two digits or more; no other address is accepted.
Each formatter either refuses or writes a NUL-terminated string of the length it returns inside the capacity it was given.
The firmware formatter prints any value as its whole part, '.', and three digits, also when the whole part has two digits.
The box family is the one the last accepted REAC-version record names in the documented table, and UNKNOWN with no such record or one no row names.

reac_box_name refuses a NULL name buffer or a bad width, and with good widths succeeds exactly when each buffer holds its string; the name is the sent name or family stem plus the two-digit widths, the token is the name lower-cased with its first '-' dropped, the display is "<name> (<in> in / <out> out)", and the catalogue defect mask flags exactly a width or display mismatch.
The documented refusals of NULL arguments hold.
init starts a knock that listens, has no licence, and opened at the start time.
A step answers NONE or DRIVE; DRIVE comes at most once and with the licence set, and only at least REAC_KNOCK_LISTEN_NS after the wire came up and after the last frame heard.
The licence is not withheld: a step at or after that time, with nothing heard since and no licence yet granted, drives.
granted is set exactly when DRIVE has come, and a later frame does not revoke it; the state is PROVEN after DRIVE, else CANCELLED after a frame, else LISTENING.
Open accepts exactly a file of at least 24 bytes with one of the two classic magics, notes the byte order, and a reader that failed to open holds no stream.

Each record handed back fits the buffer, is the file's next record that fits and is not empty, with the original length, and an 802.1Q tag stripped exactly when the record carries one, its VID kept; reading stops within one record per 16 bytes of file.
The timestamp of each record handed back is the record header's seconds and microseconds.
The walk ends with 0 exactly at the end of the file and with -1 on a cut record or header, never with any other answer.
After close the reader holds no stream and answers -1; it reopens, and the reopened reader gives the same first answer as before.
The step builder accepts exactly a body of REAC_SCENE_BYTES and a step in [0, REAC_SCENE_STEPS), refuses everything else, and a refused step writes nothing into the block.

A built step is a cd ea link-1 bulk block whose bytes sum to zero, carries its FIRST, MIDDLE or LAST segment, declares its share of the body and carries the body's bytes at that offset; the LAST step ends with the fixed 12-byte trailer.
reac_ctrl_parse reads every built step back as SCENE_TRANSFER with the link, segment, opcode and length it was built with, and its block checksum check accepts it.
A whole body is accepted at every step, the step payloads concatenated in order are the body byte for byte, and their lengths sum to the total the first step declares.

set_mac and scene_build each accept exactly a REAC_SCENE_BYTES body, and a refused call writes nothing; set_mac writes the MAC at REAC_SCENE_MAC_OFF and nothing else, and scene_build makes the body zeros, the three tags and the MAC.

If an injected malloc failure happened during xmlRegexpCompile, it must return NULL (one direction only: a spurious NULL is not flagged).
Pull parser (xmlCtxtReadMemory) and push parser (xmlParseChunk with fuzzed chunk size) agree on success vs failure (errNo == XML_ERR_OK) whenever neither hit OOM/IO.
When both parsers succeed (and XML_PARSE_NOBLANKS is off), the xmlSaveDoc serializations of the pull-parsed and push-parsed documents are byte-identical.
OOM reporting contract for xmlXPathContextSetCache and xmlXPtrEval (lastError.code == XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY iff an injected failure occurred). The document is parsed before injection is armed.
lua_stringtonumber failure (returns 0) leaves the stack unchanged
LZ4_compress_default into a fuzzed capacity in [0, LZ4_compressBound]; if it returns >0, LZ4_decompress_safe must regenerate exactly size bytes equal to the input.
LZ4_compress_HC at a fuzzed level (LZ4HC_CLEVEL_MIN..MAX) into a fuzzed capacity in [0, size]; if it returns >0, LZ4_decompress_safe must regenerate the input exactly.
LZ4_compress_default into a bound-sized buffer must succeed and LZ4_decompress_safe must regenerate exactly the input.
Partial-decompression law: LZ4_decompress_safe_partial with targetOutputSize = a fuzzed partialCapacity in [0, size] must return exactly partialCapacity bytes equal to the input's prefix.

For compressible input (compressed_len < size), lzo1x_decompress into size+1 bytes must return LZO_E_OK and produce exactly size bytes. ONLY THE LENGTH is compared: the decompressed content is never memcmp'd against the input, so a decoder that returned the right number of wrong bytes would pass.
Encoded size is within the advertised bound: 0 < res <= meshopt_encodeVertexBufferBound(count, stride)
Determinism: re-encoding the same input into a buffer of exactly res bytes placed at the end of the allocation returns the same size (and exercises encoder bounds safety)

Meshlet index round trip modulo rotation: encodeMeshlet(triangles) then decodeMeshlet (both 4-byte and 3-byte triangle outputs) returns every triangle equal to the input triangle up to a cyclic rotation (abc, bca or cab)
Meshlet vertex round trip: 32-bit vertex references decode back exactly, and the 16-bit decode equals the low 16 bits of each input reference
deflate(Z_NO_FLUSH) with ample output space must consume all input ('deflate not greedy' -> exit 1)
deflate(Z_FINISH) after feeding its own compressed output back in must report Z_STREAM_END; deflateInit/deflate/deflateEnd must return Z_OK
The deflate stream just produced must inflate to Z_STREAM_END without any inflate error (output discarded, not compared)
Deflate the input with 1-byte in/out buffers, inflate it back with 1-byte buffers, and the result must equal the input byte-for-byte (memcmp over dataLen)
abort() if one of the four built-in GFM extension names is not registered; input-independent setup check, trivially true once LLVMFuzzerInitialize registered the core extensions.

allocator ownership: the harness installs counting malloc/realloc/free wrappers (1 GiB cap) and aborts if libcbor ever frees or reallocs a pointer the wrapper did not hand out (catches double free / foreign free even in a plain build)

canonicalisation is a fixpoint: decode(input) -> encode = buf2 (canonical form); decode(buf2) -> encode must give the same length and the same 32-bit xorshift checksum as buf2, for each of the AllTypes schemas (proto2/proto3 x static/pointer)
nestegg_read_packet contract: when it returns <= 0 (end of stream or error) it must not hand back a packet (pkt stays NULL)
The manifest and URI followed after their NUL by a name character or by NULs get the same answer: the reader reads nothing past either string.
The reader holds at most the URI's length plus 3 bytes.
The reader says the manifest names the URI exactly when the harness's own reading of the stated rule does, including the limit of 16 namespace declarations read.
Whatever the answer, the reader gives back every byte it allocated, also when asked with its allocation failing.

The empty text names nothing; a manifest written from the URI as "<uri>", and at each split into a namespace and a plain local name as an @prefix, a SPARQL PREFIX or an empty-prefix declaration with its prefixed name, names it; the same spellings with one more name character answer as the rule says.

The file read from three copies followed by different bytes ('1', '2', NUL) gets the same answer each time, and the same tree whenever two of them are accepted: the reader reads nothing past the end of the file. The three are compared only when memory did not run out; a reading that ran out must be refused cleanly instead.
While reading a file of n bytes the reader holds at most 256 n bytes plus a constant for the 32 open containers and 4096 more.

The reader accepts exactly the files the harness's own grammar reads (JSON with nesting at most 32 deep, no \u0000, surrogates only in pairs, the stated number form), and reads each to the tree the harness reads from it: types, member names in order, string bytes, number text and value.
A refused file leaves the tree all zero bytes and gives back every byte the reader allocated while refusing it.

The file read again with one of its allocations failing is refused cleanly in the same way; a write, pretty or compact, with one of the writer's allocations failing returns no text and holds no memory.
An accepted tree written compact and pretty is, byte for byte, the harness's rendering of the writer's format, and reads back to the same tree.

Setting modifiedAt on an accepted object, then writing and reading it back, keeps every other member with its name, value and place, sets an existing modifiedAt in place or appends a new one, and holds the value set.
The text decoded from three copies with different bytes after its NUL gets the same answer each time, and the same bytes whenever two of them decode: the decoder reads nothing past the NUL.
For a text of n characters the decoder holds at most n / 4 * 3 + 3 bytes.
The decoder refuses exactly the texts the harness's own reading of RFC 4648 base64 refuses, and decodes every other text to the bytes the harness reads from it.
A refused text returns no body, leaves the length it was handed unwritten, and gives back every byte the decoder allocated.
Any text decoded with its allocation failing is refused cleanly in the same way, and a body encoded with the encoder's allocation failing returns no text and holds no memory.

A decoded body encodes to the padded RFC 4648 text of (len + 2) / 3 * 4 characters, letter for letter the harness's own encoding, equal to the input when the input (without whitespace) is already that encoding, and decodes back to the same bytes.
The encoded body set as state.bytes of a preset document, written and read back, decodes to the same bytes.
A ring takes a line exactly when the order is 3 or 5 and the ring is longer than the kernel's reach. A refusal returns the code that names its cause and leaves the line unarmed.
An unarmed line reports a latency of 0 and leaves the block unchanged, bit for bit.
The delay delivered is finite and inside the ring's longest delay, and a non-finite request reads as 0. The delay also equals the harness's own reading of the rule in the library's comment.
Every sample from the fractional line is finite and no larger than the absolute sum of the Lagrange weights times the take's peak.
A whole-sample delay outputs the take delayed by that many samples, bit for bit, with zero before the take starts.
A fractional delay outputs the Lagrange sum, computed by the harness over its copy of the take, to within a tolerance scaled by the weights and the peak.

omx_idelay_samples is inside the ring. It is the rounded delay saturated at the ring's last slot, and 0 for a delay of no length. This holds both for any finite ms and rate and for the grid's ms and declared rates.
A steady integer delay on either leg outputs the take delayed, bit for bit.
While the integer delay moves, each sample on either leg stays between the old tap and the new tap it fades across.
At the end of the input, no contract of the library is recorded as broken. The ledger is emptied after the calls whose PRE the harness breaks on purpose.
The head filters write at most four sections. Each section is stable (Jury conditions, computed by the harness) and has finite numerator coefficients.
The bank has at most as many sections as bands, exactly one per band that is on, and none when the EQ is off.
Every section of the bank is stable by the harness's own reading of its coefficients, and every coefficient is finite.

Section i belongs to the i-th band that is on. It is parked exactly when that band is a peaking or shelf band at 0 dB, and its gain at DC matches the band kind's closed form to a relative tolerance of 1e-3.
The bank's magnitude in dB is finite at every frequency asked, and it is exactly 0 dB when no section is live.
The cascade gives finite samples for finite samples. A bank with no live section leaves the block unchanged, bit for bit, on each leg it runs.
The bandwidth-to-Q conversion gives a finite Q that is not negative for any finite width above 0. The octaves-to-Q conversion gives a finite positive Q for any finite width.
After each stage, no contract of the library is recorded as broken. rate-is-declared is skipped at a rate that is not declared.
Two inits of the same face at the same rate return the same answer.

After init, after each resolve and after each run, no PRE, POST or invariant contract of the library is recorded as broken. Two tokens are skipped: rate-is-declared at a rate that is not declared, and bands-partition-unity. The ledger is not read in hostile mode.
Running a block in place gives the same samples, bit for bit, as running it out of place on a twin instance that got the same ports.
When init refused the rate, run() is the identity, bit for bit, whatever the ports say.
An instance that accepted its rate and was given finite samples returns only finite samples, at any port value.
omx_clampf, omx_clamp_or and omx_unit land inside their travel for any word. A word already inside comes back unchanged, and a non-finite word given to omx_clamp_or reads as the declared default.

dB to linear is never negative and, inside +-150 dB, finite and positive, in both the libm and polynomial forms. Linear to dB keeps its floor and stays finite for any finite word; the polynomial form stays finite.
Inside +-150 dB, converting dB to linear and back gives the original dB to within 0.01 dB.
The pan law is constant power: the squares of the two legs add up to 1 (to 1e-5) on [-1, 1].

The balance law never boosts: both legs are in [0, 1] and one of them is 1, at any pan word. The fader coefficient is finite and not negative, and 0 when the strip or the DCA is muted, for a fader level on a 16-bit grid of [-200, 60] dB and send and DCA gains capped at 1e6.
A ramp starts at the applied value (0 when that is not finite), never leaves the span of its two ends, and ends on its target.

For samples on a 16-bit grid of [-8, 8], the wet/dry mix lies between the dry and wet samples, to 1e-5. For bodies on a 16-bit grid of [-4, 4], each cross-fade sample lies between the outgoing and incoming bodies, to 1e-5.

The time and corner constructors give a pole in [0, 1) for any finite argument, and a rescaled pole stays in [0, 1]. For a state and an input on a 16-bit grid of [-4, 4], one filter step lies between the input and the state (to 1e-5), and the step returns the new state.
After each call, no contract of the library is recorded as broken, except the crossover token bands-partition-unity, which this harness never reaches.

A call writes no more messages than it has room for. Each message is a channel message with 7-bit data bytes, a note on has a velocity of 1 or more on a channel the leg takes, and a note off is for a key the model has sounding.
The leg the harness builds from the first bytes is one the library accepts as valid.

A note on that the leg takes, with a transposed key inside 0..127, is delivered. Every delivered note on is inside the leg's key range and makes one message, or two when its key was held. The last message sounds the transposed key, and out_of_range equals the harness's own count.
set_leg accepts a leg exactly when the harness's own reading finds it valid. An accepted leg becomes the policy, and a refused one leaves the old policy.
release_all writes no more than its cap and only note offs. Afterwards nothing is held and the model has nothing sounding.
After each record, held_count equals the held table's population, and the table holds as many keys as the harness's own count of what was played.
The release at the end of the input leaves nothing held and no note sounding in the model.
Every velocity curve maps each velocity 1..127 into 1..127, and the linear curve is the identity.
At the end of the input, no contract of the library is recorded as broken.
The plan is refused exactly when a rate is 0 or the reduced interpolation factor (computed with the harness's own gcd) exceeds the limit.
The plan is the reduced ratio: gcd(l, m) is 1 and l times the source rate equals m times the destination rate.
The take run in the blocks the input gives yields the same samples, bit for bit and in the same count, as the take run whole.
Without a flush, no more samples come out than a whole file's frames plus half the filter length. No take makes more samples than the capacity of what went in.
Every output is finite and no larger than the input's peak times the table's worst per-phase absolute coefficient sum.
An identity plan returns the input samples unchanged.
The coefficients of each phase of the table sum to 1, to within 1e-4.
At the end of the conversion, no contract of the library is recorded as broken. The converter states no contracts, so nothing on this path records one and the check cannot fail.
For any successfully parsed operand, print succeeds, re-parsing the printed text succeeds and re-printing succeeds (only BADOUTOFMEMORY from the payload-driven allocation budget is excused).
parse(print(parse(s))) is structurally equal to parse(s): UA_AttributeOperand_parse of the printed operand gives an operand UA_equal to the first parse.
print is a fixed point after one parse/print cycle: print(parse(print(ao))) == print(ao), full string equality.
UA_copy of any value UA_decodeBinary accepted (random type index over all UA_TYPES) compares UA_ORDER_EQ to the original under UA_order (full deep comparison).

decodeJson(encodeJson(v)) == v for any Variant v that decodeJson accepted, compared with UA_order == UA_ORDER_EQ (full deep equality); the second decode must also return GOOD (BADOUTOFMEMORY excused).
encodeJson is stable across a decode/encode cycle: the second encoding is byte-identical to the first (length and memcmp).
decodeXml(encodeXml(v)) == v for any Variant v that decodeXml accepted, compared with UA_order == UA_ORDER_EQ (full deep equality); the second decode must also return GOOD (BADOUTOFMEMORY excused).
encodeXml is stable across a decode/encode cycle: the second encoding is byte-identical to the first (length and memcmp).

BN_mod_exp (optimised) vs BN_mod_exp_simple (reference) on the same a, b, m decoded from the input; a mismatch only prints the five numbers to stdout and the function still returns 0 (the OPENSSL_assert(success) was removed by c263ea553c, 2026-07-15).

OP_FOREACH: ossl_ht_foreach_until finds the key's value iff the prediction table marks it allocated; OP_FILTER: ossl_ht_filter returns exactly 0 or 1 matching value as predicted. Only an empty table in a single-input run.
Encapsulate a random 32-byte secret to an in-harness ML-KEM key, decapsulate, compare with memcmp; a mismatch only fprintf(stderr) "mismatch on secret comparison".
After SSL_read returns n > 0 into a 1024-byte buffer, n <= sizeof(buffer) (SSL_read never reports more bytes than requested); the echo SSL_write then reuses n.
Harness bookkeeping after each state step: the current stream is non-NULL and its index is below the stream count (checks the harness's own accept/create/swap stream logic).
After SSL_read returns n > 0 into a 1024-byte buffer, n <= sizeof(buffer).
Harness bookkeeping: current stream non-NULL and index below the stream count.
Sign-then-verify with an in-harness SLH-DSA key over the input message, with context-string / message-encoding / deterministic params chosen by the input; verify failure only fprintf(stderr).

after string -> ODP key -> flow -> ODP key, the regenerated key must fit ODPUTIL_FLOW_KEY_BYTES; violation only printf's and sets exit_code=1, and LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput discards parse_keys()'s return value, so the check never fails the run
the protocol chosen from usable_protocols is a single bit (is_pow2); trivially true by construction since protocol = 1u << i
assert(number_of_bytes <= size) where number_of_bytes = (size / kSizeOfOneSample) * kSizeOfOneSample: true by integer division for every size, so it checks nothing about pffft (trivially true).

Every message gets exactly one reply, a NUL-terminated string with no earlier NUL. When a recorded call answered, the reply is that answer unchanged; otherwise it is a refusal or the "resp 0" of quit. A refusal is "resp <code>" of a declared error code, and any other reply has the shape its verb declares or mod-host's "resp 0".

A verb the daemon parses itself (its own verbs, and mod-host's remove, connect, disconnect and quit) is acted on only with an argument count its declared syntax allows, counting at most 64 words; a line passed on to every worker for the workers to refuse is exempt.

Each recorded call gets the message's words where the verb's declaration puts them (as written, as atoi reads them, or the whole line with single spaces), and add's placement and client, chain's members and their count, and pin_set's verdict are the ones the harness works out from the words. Other arguments are not checked.
A refused command (a reply with a negative code) leaves the recorded state as it was: no accepted call, no descriptor scan or other follow-up, and no quit.

A command the daemon acted on, sent again from the same state as its words joined by one space, makes the same calls with the same arguments, the same reply, the same state and host settings, and quits the same.
The reply shape each verb declares, filled in, fits one line of the protocol (4096 bytes).
After every operation each source's buffer holds at most 6000 bytes of an unfinished line, never more than its capacity, and its capacity stays under 20192 bytes.

After each read, and when a source or an instance is removed, the controller reads every complete line the source wrote that is 6000 bytes or shorter, once each, unchanged and in order; while the controller is gone nothing reaches it.
After a read, and when a source or an instance is removed, the relay has taken every byte the worker wrote to each source it still reads.

When a source goes, or an instance, or the relay shuts down, the relay writes one "param_gesture <instance> <symbol> end" line for each gesture that source's lines began and did not end (for an instance, only its own), and no other line.
An event of the daemon's own reaches the controller as one line, exactly as written, and after each operation the controller has read no line the reference does not account for.
What the controller reads in each operation ends on a whole line: no line is cut short.
The relay sends only on the controller's socket, never on a worker's.
The relay follows each new worker socket it is handed.

if a document parsed, ixmlPrintDocument must return a non-empty string, else CheckXML returns 1 (and LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput returns it); trivially true because ixmlPrintDocument always emits the <?xml version="1.0"?> prolog (ixml/src/ixml.c:404), so only an allocation failure could make it NULL
The reader writes no cell past the capacity it was given; the guard cell after the last one is unchanged.
The return is -1 or a count from 0 to the capacity, and the result reports that count with at least as many head-amp keys seen.
Every cell handed on addresses a channel of the head-amp channel space with a real parameter and a value that parameter takes.
The reader returns -1 exactly for a missing object or one that is not a Props object, and then reports no cells, keys or refusal.
The cells are exactly the well-formed ones the object carries, in the order written, up to the capacity.
Every key under the head-amp prefix that the walk reached is counted, refused ones included.
The refusal reported is the first thing wrong with a key, and none only when every key was accepted.
The parse without a result object returns the same count and writes the same cells as the parse with one.
Every socket the reader opens it closes before it returns, and it sends, receives and closes only that socket.
Each operation sends exactly the netlink requests it owes, in order and byte for byte.
A read or write that cannot be made (no name, an empty name, an alias too long, an interface with no index) opens no socket.
A read answers the reply's code, and on success the link kind and alias the reply carries, cut to the buffers.
A text written into a buffer ends in a NUL inside it, and the byte after the buffer is unchanged.
A write answers the reply's code, and refuses an alias too long for the kernel with -ENAMETOOLONG.
The verdict on an interface follows its alias (one set by the host is left alone, one of this daemon's is its own), then its link kind.
A mark answers its verdict, or the error of the read or write that stopped it, and -EINVAL with no marks or no name.
The marks kept are the interfaces this daemon marked, or found marked by an earlier run of its own, each once, at most 32; the unmark clears them all.
The pin is accepted exactly when the arguments are present, the text is not empty and the text before its first colon is a whole model token of the box-model table.
An accepted pin names the table row of its token.
The label is the text after the first colon, or the model's display name when there is none.
The catch-up budget is the lead past the qdisc's 300 microsecond delta in slots at the frame rate, rounded down, from 1 to 1000000; a frame rate of zero or less gives 1.
A Props write with no rate key returns 0 and leaves the caller's rate unchanged.
A rate key holding an Int, or a Float whose nearest integer fits an int, returns 1 and that rate (the first such key's).
A rate key with no usable number, or an object that is not a Props object, returns -1 and leaves the caller's rate unchanged.
The decision refuses a slave first, then a rate off the closed list (44100, 48000, 96000), then a rate outside the drivable mask, and accepts every other rate.
Each refusal publishes its own code from the shared vocabulary.
A rate's bit is its place in the closed list, it is in the list exactly when it has a bit, and the best drivable rate is the highest one in the mask.
The drivable list is the drivable rates in ascending order, comma separated; the length returned is the whole list's and the buffer holds as much as fits, NUL-terminated.
A Props write with no role key returns 0 and leaves the caller's role unchanged.
0 asks for the master and 1 for the slave, as an Int or a Float with that nearest integer; the first role key answers, and the parse returns 1.
Any other role value, a value that is not a number, or an object that is not a Props object returns -1 and leaves the caller's role unchanged.
The running role asserted again is no change and is applied; the other role is a change and is pending.
A refusal publishes its code from the shared vocabulary ("malformed"), and no refusal is "none".

The segments listed are the names the sections opened, each once, in the order first opened, with any past the 32-segment bound counted as overflow, as the harness's own line-by-line reading of the files predicts.
Each segment's role is the last one its files pinned, after the rule that a box with no model falls back to auto, as the harness's reading predicts.
Each segment's model is a token of the box-model table folded to lower case, kept only on a segment whose role is box.
A segment is switched off exactly when the last file to say ignore said yes, true or 1.
The role and the ignore answer of each segment name the file that gave them.
A kept refusal of a `knock` line, whatever its value, says that the knock takes no plan.
Every line the grammar cannot use is refused and counted, and the first ones (up to the kept bound) are kept.
Each kept refusal starts with its address: the file and the line, or the file alone for a rule that needed every file read.
A name no section opened has no entry and no role, ignore or model answer, for each opened name with one byte added and for the fixed name nosuch0 when no section opened it.
The declared VLANs are the segments named parent.vid that are not switched off, with a valid VLAN id, each once and within the table capacity given.
After a restamp, a frame of 18 bytes or more carries the low 16 bits of the counter at bytes 14-15, little-endian, and every other byte is unchanged.
The mute zeroes an audio frame of more than 18 bytes from byte 18 to its end and keeps bytes 0-17; any other frame is unchanged.
The gate answers the frame's width exactly when the frame is audio and its width, by the frame law, holds the slot, and -1 otherwise.
The writer writes exactly when the gate lets it; the frame then carries the low 24 bits of each sample at the braid bytes for that slot and time-sample, and every other byte is unchanged.
The answer depends only on the text's bytes: the same text followed by "0" and followed by a space gives the same period.
The period restored is the one the lock grammar gives, as parsed independently by the harness.
A reply's value depends only on the reply's bytes: the same reply followed by "0" and followed by a space gives the same value.
The value is the one the reply grammar gives (blanks, an optional sign, decimal digits, then blanks or a CR, on the first line) when it fits an int, and the running value otherwise.
Each of the five parameters is held to its range, the adaptive maximum to at least the adaptive minimum, and the margin to the ring size less 64.

The forward reader queues a REAC frame of 18 bytes or more (with broadcast-only, only one whose destination starts with 0xff) as audio when its type is 00 00 and as control otherwise, and drops every other frame.
The return relay passes exactly the REAC frames of 14 bytes or more.
The downstream listener accepts exactly the REAC frames of 18 bytes or more, untagged or behind one 802.1Q VLAN tag.

The clock meter counts exactly the REAC frames of 1000 bytes or more, untagged or tagged, reads the frame counter as the two little-endian bytes after the EtherType, and leaves the counter unchanged for a frame it skips.
For a frame of 18 bytes or more, the counter read is bytes 14-15, little-endian.
The channel width of a frame length is the frame law's (52 bytes plus 36 per channel, for an even width from 2 to 40, or 2 bytes more with an FCS residue), and no negative length has a width.
The copy reader keeps exactly the REAC audio frames of 50 bytes or more; a tagged one loses its four tag bytes and nothing else moves.

A slot is read only when the frame is audio and its width holds the slot; the 12 samples read are the ones the REAC braid layout places there, sign-extended from 24 bits; a declined read leaves the samples unchanged.

For a fuzz-selected OPC UA encodeable type (6 type groups, byte 0/1 select group/type), if Decode of the input succeeds then Encode of the decoded value must succeed, and Decode of that encoding must succeed.

decode(x)=v, encode(v)=b1, decode(b1)=v2, encode(v2)=b2: b1 and b2 must be byte-identical (length and memcmp), i.e. encode.decode is idempotent on the canonical encoding (the input itself is deliberately not compared).
A kernel policy that policydb_read accepted must still pass policydb_validate after policydb_optimize (optimisation preserves validity).

Any binary policy that was read successfully must be writable (policydb_write) and, for kernel policies, convertible to policy.conf and CIL; module/base policies must convert to CIL; an expanded base must also write and convert.
assert(strings.size() >= 2) directly after a loop that pads the vector to two entries: trivially true (the compiler removes it; the assert text is absent from the plain binary)
Decode path: binary_length_from_base64 never exceeds maximal_binary_length_from_base64, for arbitrary (mostly invalid) base64 text in char or char16_t.
Under loose last-chunk handling, a successful base64_to_binary must report exactly binary_length_from_base64 bytes.

base64_to_binary_safe with a fuzzed output-buffer size: written length <= buffer size (assert); on OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and BASE64_INPUT_REMAINDER the reported input count <= input size (abort); on INVALID_BASE64_CHARACTER the error position < input size (assert).
base64_length_from_binary(n, option) must equal the number of characters binary_to_base64 actually writes.
The size returned by Compress equals the size of the output string it wrote
Compressed length never exceeds the documented worst-case bound MaxCompressedLength(input.size())
The just-produced compressed buffer is accepted by the validator IsValidCompressedBuffer
For every compression level MinCompressionLevel()..MaxCompressionLevel(): Uncompress(Compress(input, level)) == input, full std::string equality
Uncompress of a buffer produced by Compress reports success
Harness-side: the unserialize buffer is empty before the magic is written (trivially true)
abort() if tidySetErrorBuffer returns < 0. It only fails on allocation failure, so this is a setup check rather than a property of the parser (relevant only under an allocation-failure model).

AES-SIV EncryptDeterministically with a fixed valid 64-byte key must succeed on every message: ct.value() on a non-OK StatusOr throws absl::BadStatusOrAccess (uncaught -> std::terminate) or aborts when exceptions are off. (res.value() on New(key) is the same check on a constant key, trivially true.)

After parsing the input and draining queued commands, the window's reference count is exactly 1 (only the harness's own reference), i.e. input processing leaked no window reference and did not drop one.

Every socket-setup call (usrsctp_socket, 12 setsockopt, bind, connect == 0 or EINPROGRESS, SCTP_RESET_STREAMS after the canned handshake) must succeed. All run BEFORE the fuzzed packet is injected and depend on the input only through the 8 flag bits of data[0], so this is a finite setup sanity check, not a property of the fuzzed packet.
VEP_Init returned non-NULL (AN = assert-non-NULL); trivially true for this fixed setup
lzma_lzma_preset() succeeds for the five fixed presets the first byte selects (0, 1, 5, 0|EXTREME, 3|EXTREME): trivially true for constant valid presets
Every number token delivered to the number callback has length > 0 (essentially guaranteed by the lexer)
CRC-32 combine law, per chunk (chunk size = data[0], min 1): crc32_combine_op(crc_so_far, crc32(0,chunk), crc32_combine_gen(chunk_len)) must equal crc32_z(crc_so_far, chunk).
Chunked crc32_z over the whole input (chunk size data[0]) must equal the one-shot crc32(0, data, len).
crc32_combine(crc1,crc2,len)==crc32_combine(crc1,crc1,len) and crc32_combine_op(crc1,crc2,op)==crc32_combine_op(crc2,crc1,op): trivially true, since crc1 == crc2 was just asserted.
crc32_combine(crc1, crc2, len) must equal crc32_combine_op(crc2, crc1, crc32_combine_gen(len)): the two combine APIs agree (operands swapped, but equal by the previous assert).
Chunked adler32_z over the input must equal the one-shot adler32(1, data, len).
adler32_combine(adler1, adler2, len) == adler32_combine(adler1, adler1, len): trivially true, since adler1 == adler2 was just asserted.
deflate(Z_FINISH) must report Z_STREAM_END; the dictionary id inflate asks for must equal the Adler-32 recorded after deflateSetDictionary; every other call Z_OK (CHECK_ERR). All print + return 0.

deflateInit2 (level/windowBits/memLevel/strategy from data[0]) with a preset dictionary = first data[0] bytes of the input, then inflate supplying the dictionary on Z_NEED_DICT; output memcmp-compared with the input. A mismatch only prints and returns 0.

deflate 3 bytes with Z_FULL_FLUSH, corrupt compressed byte 3, deflate the rest; inflateSync must succeed and the final inflate(Z_FINISH) must return Z_DATA_ERROR or Z_STREAM_END. Return codes only, no data comparison; failures print + return 0.
deflate must be greedy (avail_in == 0 after the first call) and Z_FINISH must return Z_STREAM_END; print + return 0.
Deflate a zero buffer, then already-compressed bytes at level 0, then the zero buffer again; inflate total_out must equal exactly 2*uncomprLen + diff. Length only; failure prints + returns 0.
deflate then inflate with 1-byte in/out buffers; output memcmp-compared with the input; a mismatch prints "bad inflate" and returns 0.
CRC-32 combine law per chunk (chunk size data[0], min 1): crc32_combine_op(crc_so_far, crc32_z(0,chunk), crc32_combine_gen(len)) == crc32_z(crc_so_far, chunk).
Chunked crc32_z over the input must equal one-shot crc32_z (exercises zlib-ng's SIMD/folding CRC kernels at arbitrary chunk boundaries).
crc32_combine(crc1,crc2,len)==crc32_combine(crc1,crc1,len) and combine_op(crc1,crc2)==combine_op(crc2,crc1): trivially true because crc1 == crc2 was just asserted.
crc32_combine(crc1, crc2, len) == crc32_combine_op(crc2, crc1, crc32_combine_gen(len)): the two combine APIs agree.
Chunked adler32_z must equal one-shot adler32_z (SIMD Adler kernels at arbitrary chunk boundaries).
adler32_combine(adler1, adler2, len) == adler32_combine(adler1, adler1, len): trivially true since adler1 == adler2.

Every zlib call must return Z_OK (CHECK_ERR -> exit(1)); deflate(Z_FINISH) into 100+2*deflateBound bytes must return Z_STREAM_END; the dictionary id requested by inflate must equal the Adler-32 recorded after deflateSetDictionary.

deflateInit2 (level/windowBits/memLevel/strategy from data[0..3]) with a preset dictionary = first data[0] bytes of the input, then inflate supplying the dictionary on Z_NEED_DICT; output must memcmp-equal the input.

deflate 3 bytes with Z_FULL_FLUSH, corrupt compressed byte 3, finish; inflateSync must succeed and the final inflate(Z_FINISH) must return exactly Z_STREAM_END (stricter than zlib's copy, which also accepts Z_DATA_ERROR and only prints); all other calls Z_OK. Return codes only, no data comparison.
deflate must be greedy (avail_in == 0 after the first call), Z_FINISH must return Z_STREAM_END, every other call Z_OK.

Deflate a zero buffer, then the already-compressed bytes at level 0, then the zero buffer at level 9/Z_FILTERED; inflate total_out must equal exactly 2*uncomprLen + diff. Output length only, content not compared.
Every deflate/inflate call must return Z_OK (or Z_STREAM_END where expected).
deflate then inflate with 1-byte in/out buffers; output must memcmp-equal the input.
ZSTD_compressBegin_advanced and ZSTD_compressBlock must never return an error for any input <= one block.
One-shot: the same frame decoded as standard zstd1 (magic prepended) and as ZSTD_f_zstd1_magicless must agree on acceptance in both directions, and when both accept, on decompressed size and bytes.
Streaming: the same comparison with one ZSTD_decompressStream call per format: both return 0 or neither; if both, out.pos equal and output bytes equal.
ZSTD_compressCCtx into compressBound bytes must succeed.
Compress the input at level 1, then decompress into a buffer strictly smaller than the input: must fail, and with exactly ZSTD_error_dstSize_tooSmall (empty input: must return 0).
Creating/loading/referencing the trained dictionary must succeed (FUZZ_ASSERT(ddict) / FUZZ_ZASSERT); near-trivially true because loading is lazy and any bytes are a valid raw-content dictionary.

The input is both the dictionary (random load method, content type auto/raw/full, loadDictionary vs refPrefix) and the data: if ZSTD_compress2 succeeds, decompression with the same dictionary must succeed, regenerate the input size and match byte for byte.
With ZSTD_dct_rawContent, compression must never fail ("Raw must always succeed!").
FSE_writeNCount must succeed within FSE_NCountWriteBound.

Build a random valid FSE normalized count (sum = 1<<tableLog), FSE_writeNCount it, append random trailing bytes, FSE_readNCount: must succeed, consume exactly the written size, and return the same maxSymbolValue, tableLog and every count.
HIST_count, HUF_buildCTable_wksp and HUF_readDTable must succeed, HUF_optimalTableLog must return <= 12, maxSymbol <= 255.

Histogram, build and write a Huffman CTable, read it back as a DTable (X1, or X2 falling back to X1), HUF_compress1X/4X then decompress: if compression produced output, decompression must succeed, regenerate the size and match. RLE and incompressible inputs (cSize == 0, or table write failure) are skipped.

Random valid sequence list (offsets within the window, optional 1 GiB raw dictionary, explicit or no block delimiters) -> the harness's own decodeSequences builds the source -> ZSTD_compressSequences with validateSequences=1 -> ZSTD_decompressDCtx: must succeed, regenerate the size and match byte for byte.
ZSTD_compressSequences must accept every generated sequence list; only dstSize_tooSmall in explicit-block-delimiter mode is excused.
ZSTD_compressCCtx into a random-size buffer in [0, compressBound]: any failure must be exactly ZSTD_error_dstSize_tooSmall.
If one-shot decompression succeeds, ZSTD_findDecompressedSize must not be an error and must be unknown or equal the decompressed size (frame-header content size vs actual).
